title: A New Neighbor
subtitle: Emma works in a coffee shop in Chicago. This morning somebody new comes in.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about meeting someone for the first time: names, where you are from, and the things people say when they say hello.
source: authored for this site; no source document
lexicalSet: an A1 naming text: the short passage is a frame for the everyday words the glossary teaches
passage: My name is Emma. I live in Chicago with my husband, Jack. We have a small apartment near a park, and I work at a coffee shop on the same street.
This morning a man comes in. I don't know him. He looks tired.
“Good morning,” I say. “What can I get you?”
“Coffee, please. Black.” He smiles. “I'm Sam. I live upstairs — I moved in yesterday.”
“Nice to meet you, Sam. I'm Emma. Are you from Chicago?”
“No, I'm from Texas. Everything here is new for me — the city, the people, the weather.”
“I'm from Ohio,” I say. “But I live here now. Ten years.”
I give him his coffee. “Here you go. It's on me today. Welcome to the building.”
“Thank you,” he says. “See you later, Emma.”

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Read again and choose the best answer.

items.explanation: She works at a coffee shop, so she makes and sells coffee.
“I live in Chicago with my husband, Jack.”

items.prompt: Why is this the first time Emma sees Sam?
options: He came to live in her building yesterday
items.explanation: He says: “I moved in upstairs yesterday.”

options: In the same building as Emma, on a higher floor
items.explanation: He moved in upstairs — so he lives above Emma.

items.prompt: Does Sam pay for his coffee?
items.explanation: “It's on me today” means Emma pays.

options: No. She is from Ohio, but she lives in Chicago now
items.explanation: “I'm from Ohio… But I live here now. Ten years.”

exercises.title: Useful Words
exercises.instructions: Choose the word or words that match the meaning.

items.prompt: When you need to sleep, you are ___.
items.explanation: Tired is when you need to rest or sleep.

items.prompt: The park is ___ my apartment. I walk there in two minutes.
items.explanation: Near means close to, not far.

items.prompt: My apartment is on the first floor. Sam's apartment is ___.
items.explanation: Upstairs is on a higher floor.

items.prompt: You give somebody a cup of coffee. You say: ___
items.explanation: Here you go is what you say when you give somebody something.

items.prompt: You don't want your friend to pay. You say: ___
items.explanation: It's on me means I pay, not you.
